subject: Mathematics
source: National Curriculum (KS1 Year 1: number and place value; addition and subtraction within 10); Spring 1 founding year: White Rose Maths Year 1 small-step titles (bridge from Autumn blocks 1-2, then Spring blocks 1-2), Tarbiyyah Primary Maths Policy and Maths Long Term Plan 2023-24

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Numbers to 10
lessons.title: Counting forwards and backwards within 10
objectives: Count forwards from 0 to 10
Count backwards from 10 to 0
starter: Say Bismillah. Count 5 objects on the screen.

teach.heading: Counting forwards
teach.note: Use a number track. Point to each number as the class chants. Pause on a number and ask: what comes next?

teach.heading: Counting backwards
teach.note: Backwards is harder than forwards. Use finger-folding and a rocket countdown. Common error: missing out 7 or 3.

teach.heading: Starting from any number
teach.note: Children practise starting from a number given by you. Ask: which direction are we going?

teach.heading: Missing numbers
teach.note: Show number tracks with gaps. Ask children to explain how they know using counting.

practice: Count from 0 to 10, then back to 0.
independent: Write the numbers from 0 to 10 in order.
lessons.homework: Count backwards from 10 to 0 to a family member, three times.
lessons.send: SEND: use a physical number line to touch. EAL: learn the number names with gestures. Stretch: count in 2s to 10.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: count, show and write numbers to 10
lessons.bigQuestion: How many ways can we show the same number?
objectives: Count up to 10 objects
Show a number on a ten frame and on fingers
Read and write numbers 0 to 10 in numerals and words
successCriteria: All: count up to 10 objects, touching each one
Most: show a number on a ten frame and write the numeral
Some: write the number word and spot the same number shown in different ways
lessons.crossCurricular: English: reading and spelling number words
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the blessings of Allah are too many to count; we start by counting carefully

keywords.def: say one number for each thing
a number written with digits, like 7
a box with 10 spaces in two rows of 5

hook.text: Which one does NOT show 6?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). D: seven fingers show 7. The others all show 6.

teach.heading: One number for each thing
bullets: The last number tells us how many.
teach.note: Model counting 8 pasta pieces, moving each one. Ask: I said 8 last. How many are there? (8.) Show a muddle where you count one twice and ask what went wrong.

teach.heading: Ten frames
teach.note: Hold up the egg-box ten frame with 7 pasta. Ask: how many without counting one by one? (5 and 2 more is 7.)

teach.heading: Numerals and words
teach.note: Read each word together. Point out 'seven' has 5 letters. Ask: which word starts with 'th'? (three).

teach.heading: Check: which shows 9?

check.why: Only A is 9. B mixes the word with 6 dots; C is 10.

teach.note: Pupils show A, B or C on fingers.

practice.q: Count the pasta the teacher shows: how many?

independent.q: Core: count out 5, then 9, then 3 pasta. Write each numeral.
Extend: write the word for 6 and for 10.
Stretch: show 7 in two different ways.
independent.a: For example: 7 on a ten frame (5 and 2); 7 fingers; the word seven

exit.q: Hold up the number word 'eight' on your whiteboard as a numeral.
Big question: show 5 in two ways.
exit.a: For example: 5 fingers and a full top row on a ten frame

lessons.homework: Count 10 things at home (spoons, shoes) with a grown-up and write the numerals.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: show 10 in three different ways.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: one more and one less within 10
lessons.bigQuestion: What happens to a number when we add one more or take one away?
objectives: Find 1 more and 1 less than a number to 10
Count forwards and backwards from any number within 10
successCriteria: All: find 1 more than a number with pasta
Most: find 1 more and 1 less on a number line
Some: explain that 1 less is the number before
lessons.crossCurricular: Qur'an: counting forwards and back through short surahs learnt
lessons.smsc: Moral: sharing one more with a friend is kind

keywords.def: the next number when we count

hook.text: I have 6 dates. My brother gives me one more. Then I give one to my sister. How many do I have now?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 6, then 7, then back to 6. One more and one less undo each other.

teach.heading: One more
teach.note: Put 4 pasta down, add one. Ask: 1 more than 6? (7). 1 more than 9? (10).

teach.heading: One less
teach.note: Take one from 8 pasta. Ask: 1 less than 3? (2). 1 less than 1? (0).

teach.heading: Counting backwards
teach.note: Count down together from 10 like a rocket. Then start from 7. Ask: what comes before 5? (4).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Pupils hold up fingers for the answer.

independent.q: Stretch: I am 1 more than 6 and 1 less than 8. What am I?

exit.q: 1 more than 7?
Big question: 1 less than 5?

lessons.homework: Count down from 10 to 0 at bedtime; say 1 more and 1 less than your age.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: find 2 more and 2 less.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: compare groups: fewer, more, same
lessons.bigQuestion: How can we tell which group has more without counting?
objectives: Compare two groups by matching
Use the words more, fewer and equal to
successCriteria: All: match two groups one to one
Most: say which group has more or fewer
Some: use 'greater than', 'less than' and 'equal to'
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: sorting and comparing objects
lessons.smsc: Moral: being fair means equal shares

keywords.def: the group with extra left over
the group with not as many

hook.text: Two plates: one has 5 big dates, one has 6 tiny raisins. Which plate has more things?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). The raisins: 6 is more than 5. Size does not change how many.

teach.heading: Match them up
bullets: The group with extras has more.
teach.note: Match 4 spoons with 6 cups. Ask: which has more? (cups). How many extra? (2).

teach.heading: Equal groups
teach.note: Match 5 with 5. Ask: is anything left over? (no) So they are equal.

teach.heading: Greater than, less than
teach.note: Show on the number line: further along is greater. Ask: which is greater, 3 or 8? (8).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Show 1 or 2 fingers.

independent.q: Core: make a group of 5 and a group of 3. Which has more?
Extend: make two equal groups of pasta.
Stretch: one group has 2 more than 6. How many?

exit.q: Greater: 9 or 6?
Big question: how do we know without counting?
exit.a: Match them one to one; the group with extras has more

lessons.homework: Make two groups of toys at home and tell a grown-up which has more.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: say how many more one group has.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Numbers to 10
lessons.title: Comparing numbers with <, > and =
objectives: Compare numbers to 10
Use the symbols <, > and =

keywords.def: bigger than; the open end faces the bigger number
smaller than; the point faces the smaller number

teach.heading: The hungry crocodile
bullets: The crocodile eats the bigger number.
teach.note: Use the crocodile story: the mouth always opens towards the bigger number. Draw the symbol large and let children copy the shape with their arms.

teach.heading: Less than
bullets: Read it: three is less than seven.
The point is at the smaller number.
teach.note: Read symbols aloud with children repeating. Show that 3 < 7 and 7 > 3 mean the same thing.

teach.heading: Equals
teach.note: The equals sign means 'is the same as', not 'the answer comes next'. Establish this early.

teach.heading: Choose the symbol
teach.note: Work through each. Ask children to say the sentence aloud in words.

independent: Write two true statements using < with the numbers 3 and 8.
exit: Write a true statement using > and the numbers 2 and 7.
lessons.homework: Make five comparison cards using any numbers to 10, and choose the correct symbol for each.
lessons.send: SEND: use a symbol card with the crocodile picture. Stretch: compare numbers to 20.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Numbers to 10
lessons.title: Ordering numbers and ordinal words
objectives: Order numbers to 10 from smallest to largest
Use first, second, third and so on

keywords.def: put in a line from smallest to biggest or biggest to smallest
words that tell the position in a line

starter: Say the number words for 3 and 7.

teach.heading: Smallest to biggest
teach.note: Use number cards. Ask: which is the smallest? Then the next smallest. Ordering means each number is bigger than the one before.

teach.heading: Biggest to smallest
teach.note: Contrast ascending and descending order. Use the words 'smallest' and 'biggest' and also 'least' and 'greatest'.

teach.heading: First, second, third
bullets: Who is first in the line?
teach.note: Line up 5 toys. Ask about positions. Note that ordinal numbers tell position, not how many.

teach.heading: Race to the masjid
teach.note: Use a simple story context. Include a mix of first to fifth and last.

practice: Which toy is 4th in the line?
independent: Draw 5 stars and colour the 3rd star.
exit: Who is first when the order is Zaynab, Hamza, Idris?
lessons.homework: Line up five toys. Name which is first, second, third, fourth and fifth.
lessons.send: SEND: use number cards that can be moved. Stretch: order numbers to 20.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: order numbers to 10 on a number line
lessons.bigQuestion: How does a number line help us put numbers in order?
objectives: Find numbers on a number line to 10
Order numbers from smallest to greatest
successCriteria: All: find a number on a number line
Most: order three numbers smallest to greatest
Some: order numbers greatest to smallest and explain
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: queues and house numbers go in order
lessons.smsc: Social: waiting our turn in order

keywords.def: numbers in order on a line
put in a line from small to big

hook.text: The numbers 7, 2 and 5 fell off the line! Where does each one go back?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 2 near the start, 5 in the middle, 7 further along.

teach.heading: The number line
teach.note: Point and count along. Ask: what is between 3 and 5? (4).

teach.heading: Put them in order
teach.note: Place 7, 2, 5 on the line. Ask: which is smallest? (2).

teach.heading: Greatest first
teach.note: Now order 9, 3, 6 greatest first: 9, 6, 3.

teach.heading: Check

check.q: Which is in order, smallest first?
check.why: 1, 3, 9. The others are not smallest first.

teach.note: Pupils show the letter.

independent.q: Stretch: choose three numbers between 4 and 10 and order them.

exit.q: Order 3, 8, 1 smallest first.
Big question: where are big numbers on the line?

lessons.homework: Make a number line 0 to 10 on paper and put 3 toys on 2, 5 and 9.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: order five numbers.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: parts and wholes
lessons.bigQuestion: How can two parts make one whole?
objectives: Find the parts and the whole
Use a part-whole model
Write a number sentence with + and =
successCriteria: All: say the two parts of a group
Most: fill in a part-whole model
Some: write the matching number sentence
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: sorting groups by colour or size
lessons.smsc: Social: a family is one whole made of many parts

hook.text: Picture a bowl of 7 fruits: 4 apples and 3 bananas. What are the parts? What is the whole?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). Parts 4 and 3; whole 7.

teach.heading: Parts and whole
teach.note: Use pasta in two colours if possible. Ask: what is the whole? (7).

teach.heading: Part-whole model
teach.note: Draw the circles. Whole at top, parts below. Ask: if parts are 2 and 6, what is the whole? (8).

teach.heading: Number sentences
teach.note: Write it together. Ask: what does + mean? (add). Read: 4 add 3 equals 7.

teach.heading: Check

check.q: Parts are 3 and 3. The whole is...

teach.note: Teams poll or fingers.

practice.q: Write the sentence for parts 1 and 8.

independent.q: Core: make parts 3 and 4 with pasta. Whole?
Extend: whole 9, one part 5. Other part?
Stretch: find two different ways to split 6.

exit.q: Parts 4 and 2: write the sentence.
Big question: what do two parts make?

lessons.homework: Split 8 spoons into two parts in different ways and say the number sentence.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: find all the ways to split 7.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: addition: add together and add more
lessons.bigQuestion: When we add, does the total get bigger?
objectives: Add two groups together
Add more by counting on
Solve a simple addition story
successCriteria: All: add two groups by counting all
Most: count on from the bigger number
Some: write the number sentence for a story
lessons.crossCurricular: English: telling number stories
lessons.smsc: Moral: giving to others; when we give sadaqah (صَدَقَة), the good grows

keywords.def: put together to find the total
start at a number and count up

hook.text: A bird has 5 seeds. It finds 3 more. How many seeds now? Tell the story with pasta.
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 5 + 3 = 8. The total gets bigger when we add more (unless we add 0).

teach.heading: Add together
teach.note: Push two groups together. Ask: how many altogether? (7).

teach.heading: Add more: count on
teach.note: Jump on the number line. Ask: why start at 5? (we already have 5).

teach.heading: A number story

model.problem: Amina has 6 grapes. Her mum gives her 2 more. How many now?

teach.note: Model reading the story and picking out the numbers.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Fingers.

independent.q: Extend: 4 cars and 3 more come. How many?
Stretch: make up a story for 2 + 6 = 8.
independent.a: For example: 2 cats, then 6 more come, 8 cats

exit.q: Big question: what happens to the total when we add 0?

lessons.homework: Make up one adding story at home with toys and tell it to a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: add three numbers: 2 + 3 + 4.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Addition within 10
lessons.title: Adding by counting on
objectives: Add by counting on from the larger number
Use a number line to add within 10

keywords.def: start at a number and count up from there
the bigger of the two numbers

starter: Write a sentence with a total of 5.

teach.heading: Do not count all
teach.note: Contrast counting all (1 to 8) with counting on. Counting on is faster. Put 6 in your head and hold up 2 fingers.

teach.heading: Use the number line
teach.note: Draw hops on the line. Each hop is one. Ask children to say the number they land on after each hop.

teach.heading: Start with the larger
teach.note: Show that starting with the larger number saves effort. Misconception: counting the starting number as one hop.

teach.heading: Practise
teach.note: Quick-fire. Children show the answer on mini whiteboards, then explain their method.

practice: Use the number line to solve 4 + 4.
Which number should you start with in 2 + 6?
independent: Draw hops on a number line for 4 + 5.
lessons.homework: Use a ruler as a number line to solve 5 + 4, 7 + 3 and 2 + 6.
lessons.send: SEND: use fingers or counters beside the number line. Stretch: add to numbers within 20.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: number bonds to 10
lessons.bigQuestion: How many pairs of numbers make 10?
objectives: Find pairs that make 10
Work in order so no pair is missed
successCriteria: All: find three bonds to 10 with a ten frame
Most: list all bonds to 10 in order
Some: use a bond to find a missing number
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: making 10 with coins and fingers
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: two hands, ten fingers: a gift from Allah to use well

keywords.def: two numbers that make a total

hook.text: Hold up both hands. Fold some fingers down. How many are up? How many are down? Do they always make 10?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). Yes: up and down always total 10. These are bonds to 10.

teach.heading: Ten frame bonds
teach.note: Fill 7. Ask: how many empty? (3). So 7 and 3 make 10.

teach.heading: Work in order
teach.note: Build the list together. Ask: what comes after 3 + 7? (4 + 6).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Show on fingers.

independent.q: Core: write all the bonds to 10 from 0 + 10 to 10 + 0.
Stretch: how many bonds are there from 0 + 10 to 10 + 0?

exit.q: Big question: name two pairs that make 10.

lessons.homework: Bond of the week: say the bonds to 10 with a grown-up using fingers, every day.
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: bonds to 9.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Addition within 10
lessons.title: Fact families: addition and subtraction
objectives: See how addition and subtraction link
Write related number sentences for three numbers

keywords.def: related addition and subtraction sentences using the same numbers

starter: Whole is 9, a part is 5. Other part?

teach.heading: Three numbers
teach.note: Show the part-whole model for 3, 4, 7. Then write the addition sentence.

teach.heading: Four sentences
teach.note: Introduce the minus sign. Point to the whole in each sentence: it is the biggest number. In subtraction it comes first.

teach.heading: Build a family
teach.note: Children write all four sentences. Check that the whole is the largest number.

teach.heading: Spot the odd one out
teach.note: Include a wrong sentence to check understanding. Ask why it cannot be true.

practice: Use 4 + 5 = 9 to write a subtraction fact.
exit: Write one addition and one subtraction sentence using 4, 5 and 9.
lessons.homework: Choose three numbers to 10 that work as a fact family and write all four sentences.
lessons.send: SEND: colour-code the whole. Stretch: write fact families with numbers to 20.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Place value within 20; addition and subtraction within 20
lessons.title: Bridge: subtraction: take away and find a part
lessons.bigQuestion: How are adding and taking away linked?
objectives: Take away to subtract
Find a missing part
Write a fact family
successCriteria: All: take away and say how many are left
Most: find a missing part of a whole
Some: write four facts in a fact family
lessons.crossCurricular: Everyday life: eating some of a snack
lessons.smsc: Moral: not wasting food; take only what we need

keywords.def: add and subtract facts made from the same three numbers

hook.text: There were 8 biscuits. Now there are 5. What happened?
hook.a: Begin with bismillah (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ). 3 were eaten or taken away: 8 - 3 = 5.

teach.heading: Take away
teach.note: Remove pasta one at a time. Ask: how many left? (5).

teach.heading: Find a part
teach.note: Use the part-whole model. Ask: 8 - 6? (2).

teach.heading: Fact family
teach.note: Show 3 numbers make 4 facts. Ask: what is 7 - 2? (5).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Fingers.

independent.q: Extend: write the fact family for 3, 6, 9.

exit.q: Big question: 4 + 3 = 7, so 7 - 3 = ?

lessons.homework: Bond of the week: practise 'ten take away' facts with fingers (10 - 1 to 10 - 9).
lessons.send: SEND: count real pasta with the teacher, one at a time, and point to each. EAL: say the number word, then show it on fingers. Stretch: find all subtraction facts from 10.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Subtraction within 10
lessons.title: Subtracting by counting back
objectives: Subtract by counting back on a number line
Use bonds to 10 to subtract

keywords.def: start at a number and count down
how much bigger or smaller one number is than another

starter: Say the number bonds to 10 for 4 and 7.

teach.heading: Count back
teach.note: Use fingers: count back 3 as you fold 3 fingers. Do not count the starting number as the first step.

teach.heading: Number line hops
teach.note: Draw backward hops. Ask children to say each number as they land.

teach.heading: Use bonds to 10
teach.note: Link subtraction to number bonds. This is a powerful way to remember subtraction from 10.

teach.heading: Which method?
teach.note: Discuss which method suits which question: 9 - 2 count back; 10 - 6 bonds. Encourage flexibility.

independent: Draw hops on a number line for 8 - 5.
lessons.homework: Draw a number line from 0 to 10 and show 9 - 4 and 7 - 2 with hops.
lessons.send: SEND: use a physical number line and a counter. Stretch: counting back from numbers to 20.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Subtraction within 10
lessons.title: Missing number problems
objectives: Find missing numbers in addition and subtraction sentences
Use inverse operations to check

keywords.def: a number we have to find, shown by a box or blank
the opposite operation that undoes another

teach.heading: Find the missing number
teach.note: Use cubes or a part-whole model. 4 is a part, 9 is the whole, the missing number is the other part.

teach.heading: Missing at the start
teach.note: Children often struggle when the blank is first. Return to the part-whole model.

teach.heading: Subtraction blanks
teach.note: Use counting back or fact families. Check by adding: 6 + 3 = 9.

teach.heading: Equals on the left
teach.note: Reinforce that equals means 'the same as'. Show a balance scale picture.

independent: Make up two missing number questions for a partner.
lessons.homework: Write five missing number questions, with answers on the back, for someone in your family.
lessons.send: SEND: use a part-whole model with counters for each question. Stretch: missing numbers within 20.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Subtraction within 10
lessons.title: Word problems and review
objectives: Solve one-step addition and subtraction word problems within 10
Choose whether to add or subtract

keywords.def: the total of all the groups
